title: Chain of Thought Still Thinks Fast: APriCoT Helps with Thinking Slow

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring the intrinsic baseline probability of tokens corresponding to multiple-choice answers (e.g., A, B, C, D) using cloze prompting, and calculating the correlation between these baseline probabilities and the model's overt answer choices on the MMLU benchmark under counterfactual prompting.

Evaluating how standard Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting exacerbates initial token probability preferences by forcing the model to rationalise an early heuristic selection, measured via correlations between BRP and post-CoT answer choice distributions.
